key_insight: HQNS makes dense QUBO optimization NISQ-friendly by solving the problem in rotating small quantum frontiers instead of one monolithic circuit.
engineering_relevance: The framework cuts circuit width and two-qubit interactions from O(N^2) to O(F^2) per stage, enabling larger combinatorial problems to fit current hardware limits.
method: Select a small active frontier of F variables per stage
Freeze non-frontier variables into reduced QUBO coefficients
Rotate frontiers stochastically across stages to refine a global solution
evidence_signal: On MDSSP up to N=1000, HQNS matched 99.9908% of the mean diversity score of an 11-restart parallel SA baseline while reducing wall-clock time by 65.03%, peak CPU by 55.97%, and peak memory by 35.21%.
watch_item: Performance depends on frontier size, warm-starts, CVaR filtering, and stochastic rotation, so tuning and reproducibility may be sensitive.
paper_title: Hybrid Quantum Neighborhood Selection: NISQ-Compatible Combinatorial Optimization via Stochastic Frontier Decomposition
